nodes.statement_short: Cover by an $\tilde\varepsilon$-net, apply Hoeffding's inequality to each shrunken/enlarged net ball and a union bound, then sandwich any ball between net balls.

nodes.statement:
For each of the $B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ , we  consider our sample set as $n$ i.i.d random variables   $Z^p_j$ which return the value $1$ if the sample lies within $B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ and $0$ if not.
Naturally, we get for all $j$ that
\[
\Pr[z_j^p = 1] = \int\limits_{B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)} d\nu 
\] 
Applying Hoeffding's inequality for each of the $B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ we arrive at
\begin{equation} \Pr[\overline{Z}^p - \mathbb{E}[\overline{Z}^p] \leq -\varepsilon] \leq e^{-2 n \varepsilon^2}
,    
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} \Pr[\overline{Z}^p - \mathbb{E}[\overline{Z}^p] \geq \varepsilon] \leq e^{-2 n \varepsilon^2}
,    
\end{equation}
where
\[
\overline{Z}^p = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n Z_j^p.
\]
As a result
\[
\mathbb{E}[\overline{Z}^p] = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n\Pr[Z_j^p = 1] =
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n\int\limits_{B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)}d\nu
,\]
and
\begin{equation} \mu_{min} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)) \leq \mathbb{E}[\overline{Z}^p] \leq \mu_{max} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho))
.\end{equation}
Plugging this into \eqref{eq:HoeffingtonInequality1_clean} we get
\begin{equation} \Pr\left[\overline{Z}^p - \mu_{max}\mathrm{Vol}\left(B_d(p, (1- \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)\right)\leq -\varepsilon\right] \leq e^{-2n \varepsilon^2}
,\end{equation}
or, alternatively, since $\#|X \cap B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)| = n \cdot \overline{Z}^p$ we get
\[
\Pr\left[\#|X \cap B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)| \leq n(\mu_{max}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))-\varepsilon)\right]\leq e^{-2n \varepsilon^2}
.\]

Denoting by $A_p$ the event $\#|X \cap B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)| \leq n(\mu_{max}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))-\varepsilon)$ we use the union bound to achieve 
\begin{equation} \Pr\left(\bigcup\limits_{p\in\Xi} A_p\right) \leq \sum\limits_{p\in\Xi} \Pr\left(A_p \right) \leq \ceil{ 3R/\tilde\varepsilon}^d \cdot  e^{-2n \varepsilon^2}
.\end{equation}
Explicitly, the chances that there exists $B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ containing \textbf{less} sampled points than $n(\mu_{max}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))-\varepsilon)$ are less than $c \cdot e^{-2n \varepsilon^2}$, where $c = \ceil{ 3R/\tilde\varepsilon}^d$.
Going back to $B_d(x_0, \rho)$, we know that there exists a point $\tilde p\in \Xi$ such that 
\[
B_d(\tilde p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)\subset B_d(x_0, \rho)
.\]
As a result, for any $\delta, \varepsilon, \rho$ there exists $N$ such that for all $n>N$
\[
\#|X \cap B_d(x_0, \rho)| > n(\mu_{max}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d((1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))-\varepsilon)
= n(\mu_{max}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot(1-\tilde\varepsilon)^d\rho^d-\varepsilon)
,\]
with probability larger than $1-\delta$, where
\[
\mathrm{V}_d = \frac{\pi^{d/2}}{\Gamma(d/2+1)}
.\]
nodes.name: Union bound: lower count
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over the net, then lower bound for any ball containing a net ball.
nodes.section: 8.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume

nodes.statement: \Pr\left(\bigcup\limits_{p\in\Xi} A_p\right) \leq \sum\limits_{p\in\Xi} \Pr\left(A_p \right) \leq \ceil{ 3R/\tilde\varepsilon}^d \cdot e^{-2n \varepsilon^2} .

nodes.statement:
Similarly, instead of considering $B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ we look at $B_d(p, (1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ for $p\in\Xi$ and alter the definitions of $Z^p$ accordingly.
Then, by plugging the left inequality of \eqref{eq:EzBounds_clean} into \eqref{eq:HoeffingtonInequality2_clean} we get
\[
\Pr[\overline{Z}^p - \mu_{min}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d((1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))\geq \varepsilon] \leq e^{-2n\varepsilon^2} 
\]
Utilizing the union bound once more we get the same bound as in \eqref{eq:UnionBoundAp_clean}. 
In other words, the chances that there exists a $B_d(p, (1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ containing \textbf{more} sampled points than $n(\mu_{min} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(B_d((1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)) + \varepsilon )$ are less than $\ceil{3R/\tilde\varepsilon}^d\cdot e^{-2n\varepsilon^2}$.

Going back to $B_d(x_0, \rho)$, we know that there exists a point $\tilde p\in \Xi$ such that 
\[
B_d(x_0, \rho) \subset B_d(\tilde p,(1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)
,\]
and for $\tilde\varepsilon$ small enough
\[
B_d(\tilde p,(1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho) \subset \Omega
.\]
As a result, for any $\delta, \varepsilon, \rho$ there exists $N$ such that for all $n>N$
\[
\#|X \cap B_d(x_0, \rho)| < n(\mu_{min}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d((1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))+\varepsilon)
= n(\mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot(1+\tilde\varepsilon)^d\rho^d+\varepsilon)
,\]
with probability larger than $1-\delta$.
nodes.name: Upper count
nodes.statement_short: Same with enlarged balls for the upper bound.
nodes.section: 8.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume

nodes.statement:
Finally, we get that for any $\delta, \varepsilon, \rho$ there exists $N$ large enough such that if $n>N$ we get
\[
n(\mu_{max}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot(1-\tilde\varepsilon)^d\rho^d-\varepsilon) < \#|X \cap B_d(x_0, \rho)| < n(\mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot(1+\tilde\varepsilon)^d\rho^d+\varepsilon)
\]
Since this is true for any $\tilde\varepsilon$, $(1+1/a)^a \leq 3$ and $(1-1/a)^a \geq 0.25$ we can choose $\tilde\varepsilon = \frac{1}{c_1 d}$ such that
\[(1 - \tilde\varepsilon)^d \geq 0.25^{1/c_1} \geq 0.5,\]
and
\[(1 + \tilde\varepsilon)^d \leq 3^{1/c_1} \leq 2,\]
and achieve
\[
n(\frac{\mu_{max}}{2}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d-\varepsilon) < \#|X \cap B_d(x_0, \rho)| < n(2\cdot \mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d+\varepsilon)
\]
nodes.name: Choose $\tilde\varepsilon$
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\tilde\varepsilon=1/(c_1d)$ to get factors $1/2$ and $2$.

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with bounded reach $\tau$ and a Riemannian metric $G$ pronounced through the chart $\varphi_p$ around a point $ p\in \mathcal{M} $ \eqref{eq:LocalChart_clean}. Let $r\in\mathcal{M}_\sigma$, and let $\mu, \mu_{\mathcal{M}}, \mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}}$ denote the uniform distribution on $\mathcal{M}_\sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^D$, $\mathcal{M}$, $T_p\mathcal{M}$ correspondingly. Denote $P_{\mathcal{M}}, P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}$ the projection operators onto $\mathcal{M}$ and $T_p\mathcal{M}$. Then $\left(P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}P_{\mathcal{M}}\right)_*\mu$ is a measure on $T_p\mathcal{M}$, and upon restricting this measure to $B_d(0,\rho)$ for some $\rho < \tau/2$ we get \[ (P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}P_{\mathcal{M}})_*\mu = \mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d} \sqrt{det(G)}\mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}} ,\] where $\mathrm{V}_d$ denotes the volume of a $d$-dimensional ball.

nodes.statement: We first note that since $\mu$ is the Lebesgue measure on $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ we have \[ \int_{\mathcal{M}_\sigma} d\mu = \int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d}\mu_{\mathcal{M}} ,\] where $\mu_{\mathcal{M}}$ is the uniform distribution on $\mathcal{M}$. Thus, \[ P_{\mathcal{M}} \mu = {\mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d}}\mu_{\mathcal{M}} .\] Now, $P_{\mathcal{M}}\mu$ is a measure defined on $\mathcal{M}$, which can be pulled back to the tangent domain $T_p\mathcal{M}\simeq\mathbb{R}^d$ in the neighborhood $B_d(p, \tau/2)$ according to Corollary \ref{cor:GraphOfFunctionTau2_clean}. If we denote the chart from $T_p\mathcal{M}\simeq\mathbb{R}^d$ to $\mathcal{M}$ by $\varphi_p$ we get \[ (P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}P_{\mathcal{M}})_*\mu = \mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d} \sqrt{det(G)}\mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}} ,\] where $G$ is the Riemannian metric expressed in this chart, and $\mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}}$ is the Lebesgue measure on $T_p\mathcal{M}$.

,\]

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a compact $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with reach $\tau$ bounded away from zero, and a Riemannian metric $G_p$ pronounced through the chart $\varphi_p$ around a point $ p\in \mathcal{M} $ \emphbrackets{see \eqref{eq:LocalChart_clean}}. Let $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ be a tubular neighborhood around $ \mathcal{M} $ of radius $ \sigma $ \emphbrackets{see \eqref{eq:Msigma}}, and assume $\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} < \frac{1}{2}$. Suppose that $\mu$ is the uniform distribution on $ \mathcal{M}_\sigma $. Let $X = \{r_1, \ldots,r_n\}$ be $n$ points sampled i.i.d from $\mu$, and denote the volume of a $d$-dimensional unit ball by $ \mathrm{V}_d = \frac{\pi^{d/2}}{\Gamma(d/2+1)} $. Denote, \begin{align} \begin{split} \mu_{\min} &= \mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d} \min_{\substack{p\in \mathcal{M}\\ x\in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(0,\sqrt{\sigma\tau}- \sigma)}} \sqrt{det(G_p(x))}\\ \mu_{\max} &= \mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d}\max_{\substack{p\in \mathcal{M} \\ x \in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(0,\sqrt{\sigma\tau}- \sigma)}} \sqrt{det(G_p(x))} .\end{split} \end{align} Then for any $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$, there is $N$, such that for all $n>N$ the following holds: For any $x_0\in T_p\mathcal{M}$ and $\rho \in \mathbb{R}^+$ such that $B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0,\rho + \sigma)\subset B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(0,\sqrt{\sigma\tau}- \sigma)$ \emphbrackets{see the red, green, and blue discs in Figure \ref{fig:ManifoldGoodDisc_clean}}, we have \begin{align*} \begin{split} &\#\{r_i|P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0,\rho) \} \leq n(2\cdot \mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d+\varepsilon) \\ &\#\{r_i|P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0,\rho+\sigma) \} \geq n \left(\frac{\mu_{max}}{2}\cdot V \cdot \rho^d - \varepsilon\right) \end{split} \end{align*} with probability of at least $1-\delta$.

nodes.statement: Note that both the minimum and maximum in \eqref{eq:mu_min_max_def} exist and finite since $ \mathcal{M} $ is compact and the determinant is continuous. We mention that since $ \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} < \frac{1}{2} $ we get that $ \sqrt{\sigma \tau} < \frac{\tau}{2} $ and the conditions of Corollary \ref{cor:measure_projecting_bounds_clean} are met. Note that \[ \#\{r_i|P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho) \} \leq \#\{r_i|P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}\circ P_{\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho) \} ,\] and from Lemma \ref{lem:sampling_density_almost_uniform_clean} combined with Corollary \ref{cor:measure_projecting_bounds_clean} we get \[ \#\{r_i|P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}\circ P_{\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho) \} \leq n(2\cdot \mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d+\varepsilon) .\] Thus, the first inequality is achieved. On the other hand, \[ \#\{r_i|P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho+\sigma) \} \geq \#\{r_i|P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}\circ P_{\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho)\} .\] Using again Lemma \ref{lem:sampling_density_almost_uniform_clean} combined with Corollary \ref{cor:measure_projecting_bounds_clean} we get \[ \#\{r_i|P_{T_p\mathcal{M}}\circ P_{\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho)\} \geq n \left(\frac{\mu_{max}}{2}\cdot \mathrm{V}_{d} \cdot \rho^d - \varepsilon\right) ,\] and the second inequality holds.

Then, for any $\alpha \leq \alpha_c$ where $\alpha_c$ is a constant depending only on $c_{\pi/4}$ of Lemma \ref{lem:M_is_locally_a_fuinction_clean}, there is $M$ such that for $\tau/\sigma >M$ (see assumption \ref{assume:noise} in Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions}) we have \[ \angle_{\max}(H_0, T_0 f_{-1/2}) \leq \frac{3\alpha}{2} .\]

Let $g_0:(q_{-1},T_p\mathcal{M}) \simeq \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$ defined as $g_0(x) = \phi_p(x) + (p - q_{-1})$ (note that $ (p-q_{-1}) \in T_p \mathcal{M}^\perp$ and thus this can be understood with some abuse of notation). From Corollary \ref{cor:GraphOfFunctionTau2_clean}, $\Gamma_{g_0, q_{-1}, T_p\mathcal{M}}$ coincides with $\mathcal{M} \cap \mathrm{Cyl}(p,\tau/2, \tau/2)$. We note that $\angle_{\max} (T_0g_0, T_p\mathcal{M})=0$, $\angle_{\max}(H_0, T_p\mathcal{M})\leq \alpha$ where $\alpha \leq \alpha_c$, $\|p-q_{-1}\| \leq \sigma$ and from assumption \ref{assume:noise} in Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions}, we have that $\sigma \leq \frac{3\tau}{4 \cdot 16}$. nodes.statement: We find $\kappa$ that will satisfy \eqref{eq:n_bound1_kappa_lem}. Recalling that $\delta_1 = \frac{\delta}{2\kappa}$, we have that \[ C_0 \left(\ln \frac{1}{\delta_1}\right) = C_0 \left(\ln \frac{2\kappa}{\delta}\right). \] Rewriting \eqref{eq:n_bound1_kappa_lem}, we need $\kappa$ to satisfy \begin{equation} 2^{\kappa-1}C_0\left(\ln \frac{2\kappa}{\delta}\right) \leq \frac{ \alpha_1}{12\sqrt{d}}n^{r_1}, \end{equation} or, taking $\log_2$ of both sides, we have \begin{equation} \kappa - 1 +\log_2(C_0 ) + \log_2\left(\ln \frac{2\kappa}{\delta}\right) \leq \log_2\left(\frac{ \alpha_1}{12\sqrt{d}}\right) + r_1\log_2(n), \end{equation} or, \begin{equation} \kappa + \log_2\left(\ln \frac{2\kappa}{\delta}\right) \leq 1 + \log_2\left(\frac{ \alpha_1}{12\sqrt{d}}\right) -\log_2(C_0 ) + r_1\log_2(n), \end{equation} To simplify the expression we denote the RHS of \eqref{eq:kappa_bound1} by $x$. Then we are looking for $\kappa$ such that \begin{equation} \kappa+\log_2\left(\ln\left(\frac{2\kappa}{\delta}\right)\right) < x \end{equation} We note that \[ \kappa = x-\log_2\left(\ln\left(\frac{2x}{\delta}\right)\right) \] satisfies \eqref{eq:kappa_bound_simplified_x} since \[ x-\log_2\left(\ln\left(\frac{2x}{\delta}\right)\right) + \log_2\left(\ln\left( \frac{2x-2\log_2\left(\ln\left(\frac{x}{\delta}\right)\right)}{\delta} \right) \right)<x \] Thus, the following $\kappa$ satisfies Eq. \eqref{eq:kappa_bound1} \begin{equation} \kappa = r_1\log_2(n) + \bar{C}_{ \alpha_1,d} - \log\left(\ln\left(\frac{2r_1\log_2(n) + 2\bar{C}_{ \alpha_1,d}}{\delta}\right)\right) \end{equation} where \[ \bar{C}_{ \alpha_1,d} = 1 + \log_2\left(\frac{ \alpha_1}{12\sqrt{d}}\right) -\log_2(C_0 ). \] We now bound $ \alpha_1 2^{-\kappa}$ by \begin{equation} \begin{array}{ll} \alpha_1 2^{-r_1\log_2(n) - \bar{C}_{\alpha_1,d} + \log\left(\ln\left(\frac{2r_1\log_2(n) + 2 \bar{C}_{\alpha_1,d}}{\delta}\right)\right)} &= \alpha_1 n^{-r_1}2^{-\bar{C}_{ \alpha_1,d}}\left(\ln\left(\frac{2r_1\log_2(n) + 2\bar{C}_{ \alpha_1,d}}{\delta}\right)\right) \\ & = \alpha_1 2^{-\bar{C}_{\alpha_1,d}} n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(2r_1\log_2(n) + 2\bar{C}_{ \alpha_1,d}\right)+\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)\right)\\ & \leq C_{ \alpha_1,d} \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1} \end{array} \end{equation} Since $\alpha_1$ is bounded from above, there is $ C_{d}$ independent of $\alpha_1$ for which \begin{equation} \alpha_1 2^{-\kappa} = \alpha_1 2^{-r_1\log_2(n) - \bar{C}_{ \alpha_1,d} + \log\left(\ln\left(\frac{2r_1\log_2(n) + 2 \bar{C}_{ \alpha_1,d}}{\delta}\right)\right)} \leq C_{ d} \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1} \end{equation}

Let $\wtilde f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^{D-d} $ be the regression function defined in \eqref{eq:ftilde_def_general}. For any $\varepsilon>0$, denoting $\alpha = \angle_{\max}(H, T_0 f)$, there is a constant $C_\tau$ large enough such that for $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma} >C_\tau\sqrt{D \log D}$, and $\alpha \leq \frac{3}{2} \sqrt{C_M/M}$, where $C_M$ is from Theorem \ref{thm:Step1}, we have \[ \|\mathcal{D}\wtilde{f}(0) - \mathcal{D} f(0)\| < \varepsilon \alpha \]

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.4
nodes.statement_short: Write $\tilde f-f$ as a ratio of spherical integrals of the boundary function $g$, differentiate, and bound the two terms by concentration of measure near the equator. Key step: splitting the sphere into $\Omega_1,\Omega_2$ with $\xi=2\sqrt{\log D/D}$.

nodes.name: Recall $\Omega(x)$
nodes.statement_short: Restate the fiber $\Omega(x)$.

nodes.statement:
Next, denoting $S_{D-d}$ to be the $D-d$ dimensional unit sphere, we define $g(x, \theta):H\times S_{D-d}\to \mathbb{R}$ the maximal length from $f(x)$ in the direction $\theta$ that is inside $\Omega(x)$.
Explicitly,
\begin{equation} g(x, \theta) = \max\{y\in \mathbb{R} ~|~ (x,f(x) + y\cdot \theta)_H  \in \Omega(x)\}
.    
\end{equation}
Note, that the farthest point from $f(x)$ in $\Omega(x)$ at each direction $\theta$, by which we define $g(x, \theta)$, belongs to $\partial\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ (the boundary of the domain $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$), and is therefore exactly $\sigma$ away from some point on the manifold itself.
Since we are viewing the manifold locally as the graph of the function $f:H\to H^\perp$ we denote this point by $(\wtilde x_\theta, f(\wtilde x_\theta(x)))_H$.
Explicitly, $\wtilde{x}_\theta:H \to H$ is such that
\begin{equation} (x ,f(x) + g(x, \theta) \cdot \theta)_H^T  = (\wtilde x_\theta(x), f(\wtilde x_\theta(x)))_H^T + \sigma \vec N_\theta (x)
,\end{equation}
where $\vec N_\theta \in \mathbb{R}^D$ is perpendicular to $T_{\wtilde x_\theta}f$.
We introduced the definition of $\wtilde{x}_\theta$ here as it will be pivotal in the proofs of Lemmas \ref{lem:g_bond_weak} and \ref{lem:bound_nablag} upon which the the current proof relies.
Furthermore, we wish to stress here that by Lemma \ref{lem:bounding_stuff} $\wtilde x_\theta(0) \leq \sigma \sin (\alpha + 3 \sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\alpha)$.
Therefore, for sufficiently large $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$, $\wtilde x_\theta(0)$ is within the domain of definition of the function $f$ which by Lemma \ref{lem:M_is_locally_a_fuinction_clean} is of radius of at least $c_{\pi/4}\tau$.
nodes.name: Define $g$ and $\tilde x_\theta$
nodes.statement_short: Define the boundary distance $g(x,\theta)$ and the foot point $\tilde x_\theta$.

nodes.statement: g(x, \theta) = \max\{y\in \mathbb{R} ~|~ (x,f(x) + y\cdot \theta)_H \in \Omega(x)\} .

nodes.label: eq:g_def

nodes.statement_short: Express $\tilde f-f$ through integrals of $g$ over the sphere.

nodes.statement: \wtilde{f}(x) - f(x) = \frac{\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}\int\limits_0^{g(x,\theta)} \theta r r^{\wtilde D-1} drd\theta}{\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}\int\limits_0^{g(x,\theta)} r^{\wtilde D-1} drd\theta} = \frac{\wtilde D \int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}\theta g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D+1} d\theta}{(\wtilde D+1)\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} drd\theta} .

nodes.statement:
Next, by taking the differential of that expression with respect to $x$ we have that 
\begin{multline*}
    \mathcal{D}_{\wtilde{f}}[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[x] =
\frac{\wtilde D}{(\wtilde D+1)}\left(
\frac{(\wtilde D+1)\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}\theta g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} \nabla_x g^T d\theta}
{\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} d\theta} \right.\\
-\left.
\frac{\wtilde D\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}\theta g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D+1} d\theta \int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}} g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D-1}\nabla_x g^T d\theta}
{\left(\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} d\theta\right)^2}     
\right)
,\end{multline*}
where $\nabla_x g$ stands for the gradient of $g(\theta, x)$ with respect to the $x$ variables only.
As can be seen in the above equation there is a multiplicative factor of size $\approx (D - d)$ for both summends.
In order to deal with this obstacle we wish to utilize the fact that in high dimensions most of the volume of a sphere is concentrated near an equator.
Thus, we split the domain into two different regions that we will deal with separately (we will use this trick in few of the other proofs). 
In case $D-d$ is small, then the following computations can be done without splitting the domain into two regions (one near the equator and the the second being the remaining cap), and include the $D-d$ factor in the constant that will be cancelled by $M$.
Therefore, we assume without losing the generality of our claim that $D-d = \wtilde D > 3$.

orm{v_1}}}) = \angle(u_1, v_1) .\end{align*} Thus, \[ \angle(u_1, v_1) =  eta_1 ,\] and we can choose $ w_1 = v_1 $. \paragraph*{The induction step:} Now we assume that for all $ i\leq j $ \[ w_i =  rac{v_i}{
orm{v_i}} ,\] where \[ v_i = P_{L_2}(u_i) .\] And, we wish to show that \[ \angle(u_{j+1}, v_{j+1}) =  eta{j+1} ,\] where the fact that $  eta_{j+1} \leq \angle(u_{j+1}, v_{j+1})$ results directly from the definition of $  eta_{j+1} $. We first note that since \[ u_{j+1}\perp\mathcal{U}_j ,\] we have \[ P_{L_2}(u_{j+1})
otin Span\{P_{L_2}(u_i)\}_{i=1}^j = \mathcal{W}_j ,\] thus, \[ v_{j+1} \in \mathcal{W}_j^\perp .\] From here on we can repeat the same argument as in the basis of the induction, just replacing $ L_1, L_2 $ with $ \mathcal{U}_j^\perp, \mathcal{W}_j^\perp $ respectively.
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.6
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $i$: the principal vector $w_i$ can be taken as the normalized projection of $u_i$, by least-squares optimality of projections.

nodes.name: Recall principal angles
nodes.statement_short: Restate the definition of principal angles.

nodes.statement:
We now wish to show that for all $ i $ we can choose
	\[
	w_i = \frac{P_{L_2}(u_i)}{\norm{P_{L_2}(u_i)}}
	.\]
	Since the definition is inductive so will be our proof.
nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement_short: Show $w_i$ can be the normalized projection of $u_i$, by induction.

nodes.statement:
\paragraph*{Basis of the induction $ i=1 $:}
	We first denote
	\[
	v_1 = P_{L_2(u_1)}
	.\]
	Note that,
	\[
	\beta_1 = \angle(u_1, w_1) = \angle(u_1, \norm{v_1} w_1 )
	,\]
	and by the minimization problem defining $ \beta_1 $ we know that
	\[
	\beta_1 \leq \angle(u_1, v_1)
	.\]
	Then, since the projection onto a linear space minimizes the Least-Squares norm we get
	\begin{align*}
	\lrangle{u_1 - v_1, u_1 - v_1} 
	&\leq 
	\lrangle{u_1 - \norm{v_1}w_1, u_1 - \norm{v_1}w_1}\\
	\lrangle{u_1,u_1} - 2\lrangle{u_1, v_1} + \lrangle{v_1,v_1} 
	&\leq
	 \lrangle{u_1,u_1} - 2\lrangle{u_1, \norm{v_1}w_1} + \lrangle{\norm{v_1}w_1,\norm{v_1}w_1} \\
	 - 2\lrangle{u_1, v_1} + \norm{v_1}^2 
	 &\leq
	 - 2\lrangle{u_1, \norm{v_1}w_1} + \norm{v_1}^2 \\
	 \lrangle{u_1, \norm{v_1}w_1} 
	 &\leq
	 \lrangle{u_1, v_1}\\
	 \lrangle{u_1, w_1} 
	 &\leq
	 \lrangle{u_1, \frac{v_1}{\norm{v_1}}}
	 \\
	 \beta_1 =
	 \angle(u_1, w_1) =
	 \arccos(\lrangle{u_1, w_1}) 
	 &\geq
	 \arccos(\lrangle{u_1, \frac{v_1}{\norm{v_1}}}) = \angle(u_1, v_1)
	.\end{align*}
	Thus, 
	\[
	\angle(u_1, v_1) = \beta_1
	,\]
	and we can choose $ w_1 = v_1 $.
nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement_short: Projection minimizes least squares, so $\angle(u_1,v_1)=\beta_1$.

nodes.statement:
\paragraph*{The induction step:}
	Now we assume that for all $ i\leq j $
	\[
	w_i = \frac{v_i}{\norm{v_i}}
	,\]
	where
	\[
	v_i = P_{L_2}(u_i)
	.\]
	And, we wish to show that 
	\[
	\angle(u_{j+1}, v_{j+1}) = \beta{j+1}
	,\]
	where the fact that $ \beta_{j+1} \leq  \angle(u_{j+1}, v_{j+1})$ results directly from the definition of $ \beta_{j+1} $.
	
	We first note that since
	\[
	u_{j+1}\perp\mathcal{U}_j
	,\]
	we have
	\[	P_{L_2}(u_{j+1})\notin Span\{P_{L_2}(u_i)\}_{i=1}^j = \mathcal{W}_j
	,\]
	thus, 
	\[
	v_{j+1} \in \mathcal{W}_j^\perp  
	.\]
	From here on we can repeat the same argument as in the basis of the induction, just replacing $ L_1, L_2 $ with $ \mathcal{U}_j^\perp, \mathcal{W}_j^\perp $ respectively.
nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the base argument on the orthogonal complements.

nodes.statement: Let the conditions of Lemma \ref{lem:bound_Df-Dfwtilde} hold. Let $g(x, \theta)$ be as defined in Equation \eqref{eq:g_def}. Then, for $\alpha$ smaller than some constant and $M$ larger then some constant, \[ \sigma \leq g(0,\theta) \leq \sigma + 4\sigma \alpha^2 \]
nodes.name: Bounds on the boundary function $g(0,\theta)$
nodes.label: lem:g_bond_weak

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.7
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound from the $\sigma$-ball around $f(0)$; upper bound from the foot-point estimates of Lemma 9.15.

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement_short: The $\sigma$-ball around $(0,f(0))$ lies in $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$.

nodes.statement:
From Lemma \ref{lem:bounding_stuff} we have that 
    \[
    \|f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)) - f(0)\| \leq 2\sigma \sin (\alpha + 3\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha) \tan \alpha,
    \]
    where $\wtilde{x}_\theta$ defined in \eqref{eq:x_tilde_def}.
nodes.name: Foot-point bound
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 9.15 bounds $\|f(\tilde x_\theta(0))-f(0)\|$.

nodes.statement:
Since $(0, f(0))_H + \theta g(0,\theta)$ is at distance  $\sigma$ from $(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0), f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)))_H$, and denoting $\theta\in H^\perp\subset \mathbb{R}^D$ by $(0, \bar \theta)_H$ we have that
    \[
    \sigma  =
    \norm{(0, f(0) + \bar \theta g(0, \theta)  )_H -(\wtilde x_{\theta}(0), f(\wtilde x_\theta(0))_H}
    = \sqrt{\norm{\wtilde x_\theta}^2 + \norm{f(\wtilde x_\theta(0) - f(0)}^2 + g(0,\theta)^2 },\]
    and thus,
    \[
    g(0,\theta) \leq \sigma + 2\sigma \sin (\alpha + 3\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha) \tan \alpha,
    .\]
nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement_short: The boundary point is $\sigma$ from its foot point.

nodes.statement:
Then, for $\alpha$ smaller than some constant and $M$ larger than some constant we have 
    \[
    g(0,\theta) \leq \sigma + 4\sigma \sin^2 \alpha,
    \] 
    or,
    \[
    g(0,\theta) \leq \sigma + 4\sigma \alpha^2,
    \]
nodes.name: Simplify
nodes.statement_short: Simplify to $\sigma+4\sigma\alpha^2$.

nodes.statement: Let the conditions of Lemma \ref{lem:bound_Df-Dfwtilde} hold. Let $g(x, \theta)$ be as defined in Equation \eqref{eq:g_def}. Then, \[ \|\nabla_x{g}(0,\theta)\| \leq C \cdot \frac{\sigma}{\tau}\alpha ,\] where $\nabla_x{g}$ denotes the gradient of $g(x, \theta)$ with respect to the $x$ variables only, and $C$ is some constant.
nodes.name: Gradient bound on $g$
nodes.label: lem:bound_nablag

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.8
nodes.statement_short: Solve the quadratic defining $g$, differentiate the root, and bound each term with Lemmas 9.9, 9.12, 9.13 and 9.15.

nodes.statement:
Following the definition of $\wtilde{x}_\theta$ in \eqref{eq:x_tilde_def} and $g(x,\theta)$ in \eqref{eq:g_def}, we have the following equations that describe the connection between $x, \wtilde{x}_\theta$ and $g(x,\theta)$
\begin{equation*}
\left(\begin{array}{c}
     \wtilde{x}_\theta \\
     f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) 
\end{array}\right)
+
\sigma \vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) = 
\left(\begin{array}{c}
     x \\
     f(x) 
\end{array}\right)_H
+ 
\left(\begin{array}{c}
     0 \\
     \bar \theta
\end{array}\right)_H g(x,\theta)
,\end{equation*}
where $\theta\in \mathbb{R}^D$ is written as $(0, \bar \theta)_H$, and $ \vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta)\in \mathbb{R}^D$ is some unit vector perpendicular to $T_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}f$.
Explicitly, 
\begin{equation} \vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) \perp T_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}f
,\end{equation}
and 
\begin{equation} \|\vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) \| = 1
.\end{equation}
Alternatively, we can write,
\begin{equation} \sigma \vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) = 
\left(\begin{array}{c}
     x \\
     f(x) 
\end{array}\right)_H
-
\left(\begin{array}{c}
     \wtilde{x}_\theta \\
     f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) 
\end{array}\right)_H
+ 
\left(\begin{array}{c}
     0 \\
     \bar \theta
\end{array}\right)_H g(x,\theta)
\end{equation}
nodes.name: Defining equations
nodes.statement_short: Write the equations linking $x$, $\tilde x_\theta$ and $g$.

nodes.statement: \vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) \perp T_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}f ,
nodes.name: Equation (86) [eq:c_2]
nodes.label: eq:c_2

nodes.statement: \|\vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) \| = 1 .
nodes.name: Equation (87) [eq:c_3]
nodes.label: eq:c_3

nodes.statement: \sigma \vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) = \left(\begin{array}{c} x \\ f(x) \end{array}\right)_H - \left(\begin{array}{c} \wtilde{x}_\theta \\ f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \end{array}\right)_H + \left(\begin{array}{c} 0 \\ \bar \theta \end{array}\right)_H g(x,\theta)
nodes.name: Equation (88) [eq:c_1]
nodes.label: eq:c_1

nodes.statement:
Taking the norm of \eqref{eq:c_1} and using \eqref{eq:c_3} we have  

\begin{equation*}
\left\|\left(\begin{array}{c}
     x \\
     f(x) 
\end{array}\right)
-
\left(\begin{array}{c}
     \wtilde{x}_\theta \\
     f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) 
\end{array}\right)
+ 
\left(\begin{array}{c}
     0 \\
     \bar  \theta
\end{array}\right) g(x,\theta)\right\|^2 = \sigma^2
\end{equation*}
or,
\[
g^2 + 2g \left(\begin{array}{c}
     x - \wtilde{x}_\theta \\
     f(x) - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) 
\end{array}\right) ^T
\left(\begin{array}{c}
     0 \\
     \bar \theta
\end{array}\right)
+
\left\|\left(\begin{array}{c}
     x - \wtilde{x}_\theta \\
     f(x) - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) 
\end{array}\right)\right\|^2 
-
\sigma^2 =0
\]
or,
\[
g^2 + 2g (f(x) - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta))^T \bar \theta 
+
\|x - \wtilde{x}_\theta\|^2 
+
\| f(x) - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \|^2
-
\sigma^2 =0
\]
the two solutions are 
\begin{multline} g_{\pm}(x,\theta) =\\ -f(x)^T \bar \theta + f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta \pm
    \sqrt{\sigma^2 + (f(x)^T \bar \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta)^2 - \|x- \wtilde{x}_\theta\|^2 - \|f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \|^2}
\end{multline}
nodes.name: Quadratic for $g$
nodes.statement_short: Take norms to get a quadratic in $g$ and its roots.

nodes.statement: g_{\pm}(x,\theta) =\\ -f(x)^T \bar \theta + f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta \pm \sqrt{\sigma^2 + (f(x)^T \bar \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta)^2 - \|x- \wtilde{x}_\theta\|^2 - \|f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \|^2}
nodes.name: Equation (89) [eq:sol_g_pm]
nodes.label: eq:sol_g_pm

nodes.statement:
From Lemma \ref{lem:bounding_stuff}, for $\alpha$ smaller than some constant, we have that
\[ 
\|0- \wtilde{x}_\theta(0)\|^2 + \|f(0)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)) \|^2 \leq \sigma^2
\]
and thus, the solutions of Eq. \eqref{eq:sol_g_pm} at $x=0$ are $g_{-}(0, \theta) < 0$ and $g_{+}(0, \theta) > 0$.
Therefore, from continuity we get that there is a neighborhood of $x=0$ such that the only non-negative solution is
\begin{multline} g(x,\theta) =\\ -f(x)^T \bar \theta + f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta + 
    \sqrt{\sigma^2 + (f(x)^T \bar \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta)^2 - \|x- \wtilde{x}_\theta\|^2 - \|f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \|^2}
.\end{multline}
In addition, from the definition of $g$ the only valid solution is the non-negative one which appears on Eq. \eqref{eq:sol_g}.
nodes.name: Select the root
nodes.statement_short: Only the nonnegative root is valid near 0.

nodes.statement: g(x,\theta) =\\ -f(x)^T \bar \theta + f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta + \sqrt{\sigma^2 + (f(x)^T \bar \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta)^2 - \|x- \wtilde{x}_\theta\|^2 - \|f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \|^2} .
nodes.name: Equation (90) [eq:sol_g]
nodes.label: eq:sol_g

nodes.statement:
Thus, denoting 
\begin{equation} \Delta = \sigma^2 + (f(x)^T \bar \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta)^2 - \|x- \wtilde{x}_\theta\|^2 - \|f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \|^2,
\end{equation}
we have that near $x=0$
\begin{multline} \nabla_x{g}(x,\theta) =\\ -\mathcal{D}_f[x]^T\bar\theta + J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta} \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T \bar \theta 
    +
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}}
    \left( 
     (f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta - f(x)^T \bar \theta)\left(J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T \bar \theta - \mathcal{D}_f[x]^T \bar \theta\right) 
    \right. \\
    \left.- 
    (I_d-J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta})(x- \wtilde{x}_\theta) 
    - 
    (\mathcal{D}_f[x]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T)(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta))  \right)
,\end{multline}
where $J_{\wtilde x_\theta(x)} = \mathcal{D}_{\wtilde x_\theta (x)}[x]$ is the Jacobi matrix of the function $\wtilde x_\theta (x)$, and $I_d$ is the $d$-dimensional identity matrix.
Alternatively, we can write
\begin{multline} \nabla_x{g}(x,\theta) =\\ (J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta} \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T - \mathcal{D}_f[x]^T ) \bar\theta 
    +
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}}
    \left( 
     (f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T\bar\theta - f(x)^T\bar\theta ) \left(J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T - \mathcal{D}_f[x]^T \right)\bar\theta 
    \right. \\
    \left.- 
    (I_d-J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta})(x- \wtilde{x}_\theta) 
    - 
    (\mathcal{D}_f[x]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T)(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta))  \right)
\end{multline}
nodes.name: Differentiate
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate $g$ in $x$.

nodes.statement: \Delta = \sigma^2 + (f(x)^T \bar \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta)^2 - \|x- \wtilde{x}_\theta\|^2 - \|f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \|^2,
nodes.name: Equation (91) [eq:Delta]
nodes.label: eq:Delta

nodes.statement: \nabla_x{g}(x,\theta) =\\ -\mathcal{D}_f[x]^T\bar\theta + J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta} \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T \bar \theta + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \left( (f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T \bar \theta - f(x)^T \bar \theta)\left(J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T \bar \theta - \mathcal{D}_f[x]^T \bar \theta\right) \right. \\ \left.- (I_d-J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta})(x- \wtilde{x}_\theta) - (\mathcal{D}_f[x]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T)(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)) \right) ,
nodes.name: Equation (92) [eq:nabla_g]
nodes.label: eq:nabla_g

nodes.statement: \nabla_x{g}(x,\theta) =\\ (J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta} \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T - \mathcal{D}_f[x]^T ) \bar\theta + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \left( (f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T\bar\theta - f(x)^T\bar\theta ) \left(J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T - \mathcal{D}_f[x]^T \right)\bar\theta \right. \\ \left.- (I_d-J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta})(x- \wtilde{x}_\theta) - (\mathcal{D}_f[x]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T)(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)) \right)
nodes.name: Equation (93) [eq:nabla_g2]
nodes.label: eq:nabla_g2

nodes.statement:
Next, using Lemma \ref{lem:bound_J}, Lemma \ref{lem:Dfx-Dfxtilde} and Lemma \ref{lem:bounding_stuff}, we bound 
\begin{equation} \begin{aligned}
     \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta} \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \| &= \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]^T -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T+\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)} \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \| 
     \\
     &\leq \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]^T -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T\|+\|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)} \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \|
     \\
     &\leq \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]^T -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T\|+\|I_d - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)} \|\|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \| 
     \\
     &= \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}\sin \alpha) + \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}) \|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \|
     \\
     &= \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}\cdot\alpha) 
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
nodes.name: Bound the Jacobian term
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 9.9, 9.13, 9.15 bound the main term by $O(\alpha\sigma/\tau)$.

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta} \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \| &= \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]^T -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T+\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)} \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \| \\ &\leq \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]^T -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T\|+\|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)} \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \| \\ &\leq \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]^T -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T\|+\|I_d - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)} \|\|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \| \\ &= \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}\sin \alpha) + \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}) \|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \| \\ &= \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}\cdot\alpha) \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Equation (94) [eq:Df-JDfwtilde]
nodes.label: eq:Df-JDfwtilde

nodes.statement:
Now, using \eqref{eq:nabla_g2} and the fact that $\norm{\bar \theta} = 1$ we get
\begin{align*}
    \|\nabla_x{g}(0,\theta)\|  &\leq\|\mathcal{D}_f[0]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}[0] \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T\|  \\\
    &~~~
    +
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}}
    \left( 
     \|f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)) - f(0)\| \|J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}[0]\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T - \mathcal{D}_f[0]^T \| 
    \right. \\
    &~~~ \left.+ 
    \|I_d-J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}[0]\|\|\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)\| 
    + 
    \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]^T - J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}[0]\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T\|\|f(0)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0))\|\right)
\end{align*}
From Lemmas \ref{lem:bound_J} and \ref{lem:bounding_stuff} we know that $\|I_d - J_{\wtilde x_\theta}[0]\| =\mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau})$, $\|\wtilde x_\theta(0)\|\leq \sigma \sin(\alpha + 3\sqrt{\sigma/\tau} \alpha)$, and that $\|f(\wtilde x_\theta(0)) - f(0)\| \leq 2\sigma \sin(\alpha + 3\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\alpha)\tan(\alpha)$.
In other words, for $\alpha$ smaller than some constant we can say that $\|I_d - J_{\wtilde x_\theta}[0]\| = \mathcal{O}(\sigma/\tau)$, $\|\wtilde x_\theta(0)\|\leq \mathcal{O}(\sigma \alpha)$, and that $\|f(\wtilde x_\theta(0)) - f(0)\| \leq \mathcal{O}(\sigma \alpha^2)$.
Combining this with \eqref{eq:Df-JDfwtilde} as well, we have
\begin{align*}
    \|\nabla_x{g}(0,\theta)\| &\leq\mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}\cdot\alpha)
    +
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}}
    \left( 
    \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau}\cdot\alpha^3)
    + 
    \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau}\cdot\alpha) 
    +
    \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau}\cdot\alpha^3)\right)
\end{align*}
Since Lemma \ref{lem:Dxtildew+Dxw} gives us 
\[
 \Delta(0,\wtilde x_\theta (0)) \geq \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2
,\]
we have that $\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}}\leq \sqrt{2}/\sigma$, and 
\begin{equation*}
    \|\nabla_x{g}(x,\theta)\| =  \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}\cdot\alpha)
.\end{equation*}
nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Combine with $\Delta\ge\sigma^2/2$ (Lemma 9.12).

nodes.statement: Let the conditions of Lemma \ref{lem:bound_nablag} hold. Let $g(x, \theta), \wtilde x(x)$ be as defined in Equation \eqref{eq:g_def} and \eqref{eq:x_tilde_def} respectively, let $I_d:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ denote the identity matrix and let $J_{\wtilde x_\theta}$ denote the differential of $\wtilde x(x)$ with respect to $x$. Then, \begin{equation*} \|I_d-J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}[0]\| = \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}) .\end{equation*}
nodes.name: Jacobian of the foot point is near identity
nodes.label: lem:bound_J

nodes.statement: We begin by reiterating equations \eqref{eq:c_1},\eqref{eq:c_2}, and \eqref{eq:c_3}. Namely we have \begin{equation*} \sigma \vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) = \left(\begin{array}{c} x \\ f(x) \end{array}\right) - \left(\begin{array}{c} \wtilde{x}_\theta \\ f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \end{array}\right) + \left(\begin{array}{c} 0 \\ \bar \theta \end{array}\right) g(x,\theta) ,\end{equation*} where \begin{equation*} \vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) \perp T_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}f ,\end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} \|\vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) \| = 1 .\end{equation*} Thus, there is a vector $v(x,\wtilde x_\theta)\in \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$ with $\|v(x,\wtilde x_\theta)\| = 1$, \[ \vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta,\theta) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta] v(x,\wtilde x_\theta)\|^2 + 1}} \left(\begin{array}{c} -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T v(x,\wtilde x_\theta) \\ v(x,\wtilde x_\theta) \end{array}\right) \] or, denoting $ w(x,\wtilde x_\theta) = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{\|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T v(x,\wtilde x_\theta))\|^2 + 1}} v$, we have \[ \sigma \vec N(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta) = \left(\begin{array}{c} -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T w(x,\wtilde x_\theta) \\ w(x,\wtilde x_\theta) \end{array}\right) \] Using this pronunciation of $\vec N$ we can rewrite the above equation as \begin{equation} \left(\begin{array}{c} -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T w(x,\wtilde x_\theta) \\ w(x,\wtilde x_\theta) \end{array}\right) = \left(\begin{array}{c} x \\ f(x) \end{array}\right) - \left(\begin{array}{c} \wtilde{x}_\theta \\ f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \end{array}\right) + \left(\begin{array}{c} 0 \\ \bar \theta \end{array}\right) g(x,\theta) .\end{equation} From Eq. \eqref{eq:sol_g} in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:bound_nablag} we know that $g(x, \theta) = -f(x)^T\bar\theta + f(\wtilde x_\theta)^T\bar \theta + \sqrt{\Delta}$, near $x=0$, where $\Delta$ is defined in Eq. \eqref{eq:Delta}. Combining this with the last $D-d$ equations we get, \begin{equation} w(x,\wtilde x_\theta) =\left(f(x) - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) + \bar \theta \left(- f(x)^T \bar \theta + f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) ^T \bar \theta + \sqrt{\Delta}\right)\right) .\end{equation} Looking at the first $d$ equations of \eqref{eq:c_1_w}, we have \[ -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T w(x,\wtilde x_\theta) - x + \wtilde{x}_\theta = 0 .\] Denoting the function \begin{equation} G(x,\wtilde{x}_\theta) = -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T w(x,\wtilde x_\theta) - x + \wtilde{x}_\theta ,\end{equation} we aim at using the Inverse Function Theorem (IFT) to compute $J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}$. First, we compute $\mathcal{D}^{x}_G $ and $\mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_G$, the partial differentials of $G$ with respect to the variables $x$ and $\wtilde x_\theta$: \begin{equation*} \mathcal{D}^x_G[x, \wtilde x_\theta] = - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T \mathcal{D}^x_w[x, \wtilde x_\theta] - I_d \end{equation*} \begin{equation*} \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_G[x, \wtilde x_\theta] = - \mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta)^w - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_w[x, \wtilde x_\theta] + I_d ,\end{equation*} where $\mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta)^w \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is the tensor Hessian of $f(\wtilde x_\theta):\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^{D-d}$ projected onto the target direction $w\in \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$; that is \begin{equation} \mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta)^w = \left(\frac{\partial\left(\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T\right)}{\partial \wtilde{x}_1} w \right|\left. \frac{\partial\left(\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T\right)}{\partial \wtilde{x}_2} w \right| \cdots \left|\frac{\partial\left(\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T\right)}{\partial \wtilde{x}_d} w \right) .\end{equation} Notice that $\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_\theta]^T\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times D-d}$; therefore, $\partial_{\wtilde x_j}\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_\theta]^T\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times D-d}$ and $\partial_{\wtilde x_j}\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_\theta]^T w\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$. Next, using the IFT we have that \[ J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta} = -(\mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_{G})^{-1} \mathcal{D}^x_G = \left( I_d - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_ w + \mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta)^w \right)^{-1} \left(I_d + \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T \mathcal{D}^x_w \right) ,\] and thus \[ J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}[0] = (A(I_d-A^{-1}B))^{-1}A = (I_d-A^{-1}B)^{-1}A^{-1}A = (I_d-A^{-1}B)^{-1} ,\] where \begin{equation} A = I_d + \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \mathcal{D}^x_w[0,\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)] ,\end{equation} \begin{equation} B = \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T (\mathcal{D}^x_w[0,\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)] + \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_w[0,\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)] )+ \mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta(0))^w .\end{equation} From Lemma \ref{lem:bound_A_inv_B} we have that $\|A^{-1}B\| \leq \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}) \leq 1/2$ for $\sigma/\tau$ smaller than some constant, and thus, using the first order approximation of this term we get that there is a matrix \[\mathcal{E} = \sum_{t=2}^{\infty}(A^{-1}B)^t\] such that \[ J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta} = (I_d - A^{-1}B)^{-1} = I_d +A^{-1}B + \mathcal{E} ,\] and with \[ \|\mathcal{E}\| \leq \|A^{-1}B\| \sum_{t=1}^\infty \frac{1}{2^t} = \|A^{-1}B\| .\] Thus we have, \begin{equation} \|I_d -J_{\wtilde{x}_\theta}\| \leq 2\|A^{-1}B\| = \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}) \end{equation}

nodes.statement: We begin by noting that \[ \|A^{-1}B\| \leq \|A^{-1}\|\|B\| ,\] where \begin{equation*} A = I_d + \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \mathcal{D}^x_w[0,\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)] ,\end{equation*} \begin{equation*} B = \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T (\mathcal{D}^x_w[0,\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)] + \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_w[0,\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)] )+ \mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta(0))^w .\end{equation*} Moreover, \[ A^{-1} = (I_d + \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \mathcal{D}^x_w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)])^{-1} = I_d + \sum_{t=1}^\infty(\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T \mathcal{D}^x_w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)])^t .\] From Lemma \ref{lem:Dxtildew+Dxw} we have that $\|\mathcal{D}^x_w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)]\| = \mathcal{O}(\sin \alpha)$, where we remind the reader that $\mathcal{D}^x_w[x, \wtilde x_\theta]$ is the partial differential of $w(x, \wtilde x_\theta)$ with respect to the $x$ variables only. And, from Lemma \ref{lem:bounding_stuff}we have that $\|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]\|_2 \leq \sin (\alpha + 3\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha)$ . Thus $\|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T \mathcal{D}^x_w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)]\| = \mathcal{O}(\sin\alpha)$, and thus, for $\alpha$ smaller than some constant we have \begin{equation} \|A^{-1}\| = 1 + \mathcal{O}(\sin^2\alpha) \end{equation} Furthermore, from Lemma \ref{lem:Dxtildew+Dxw} we also know that $(\mathcal{D}^x_w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)] + \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_ w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)] ) = \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau} \sin\alpha)$ and so \[ \| \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)]^T (\mathcal{D}^x_w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)] + \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_ w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)] )\| \leq \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}\sin^2 \alpha) .\] Combining this bound with the fact that $\|\mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta(0))^w\| \leq \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}) $ shown in Lemma \ref{lem:bound_DDf} we have \begin{equation} \|B\| \leq \|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]^T (\mathcal{D}^x_w + \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_ w )\|+\| \mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta)^w\| \leq \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}) + \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}\sin^2 \alpha) . \end{equation} Finally, from \eqref{eq:bound_A} and \eqref{eq:bound_B} we have that for $\alpha$ smaller than some constant \[ \|A^{-1}B\| \leq \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}) \]

From the definition of $\mathcal{H}_v$ we know that \[ \mathcal{H}_v\ = \lim_{t	o 0}  rac{\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_	heta(0)] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_	heta(0) + tv]}{t} .\] Then, from Lemma ef{lem:alpha-beta_x_no_func} we have for small $t$ \[ \sin(\angle_{\max} (T_{\wtilde x_	heta}f,T_{\wtilde x_	heta + tv}f))\leq  rac{t}{	au}(1+	an^2 eta)+\mathcal{O}(t^2/	au^2) \] where $ eta = \angle_{\max}(T_{\wtilde x_	heta}f,H)$. Therefore, applying Lemma ef{lem:norm_from_angle} we get \[ \|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_	heta(0)] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_	heta(0) + tv] \|_{op} \leq  rac{t}{	au}(1+	an^2 eta)(1+\sin  eta) + \mathcal{O}(t^2/	au^2) ,\] and we get \[ \|\mathcal{H}_v\| \leq  rac{1}{	au}(1+	an^2 eta)(1+\sin  eta) .\] Furthermore, from Lemma ef{lem:alpha_beta_D} we know \[  eta \leq \alpha + 3\alpha\sqrt{ rac{\sigma}{	au}} ,\] and so, \[ \|\mathcal{H}_v\| \leq  rac{1}{	au}(1+	an^2 \left(\alpha + 3\alpha\sqrt{ rac{\sigma}{	au}}ight))(1+\sin \left(\alpha + 3\alpha\sqrt{ rac{\sigma}{	au}}ight)) =  rac{1}{	au} + \mathcal{O}( rac{\sin \alpha}{	au}) .\] Thus, we obtain  egin{equation} \|\mathcal{H}^w\| \leq \|w\| \left( rac{1}{	au} + \mathcal{O}( rac{\sin \alpha}{	au})ight) .\end{equation} Hence, all we are left with is bounding $\|w(0,\wtilde x_	heta (0))\|$. From Eq. \eqref{eq:def_w}, Lemma ef{lem:bounding_stuff}, and Lemma ef{lem:Dxtildew+Dxw}, we have  egin{align*} \|w(0,\wtilde x_	heta(0))\| &=\|f(0) - f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0)) + 	heta \left(- f(0)\cdot 	heta + f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0)) \cdot 	heta + \sqrt{\Delta(0,\wtilde x_	heta (0))}ight)\| \ &\leq \|f(0) - f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0))\| + \left|(- f(0) + f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0))) \cdot 	hetaight| + \sqrt{\Delta(0,\wtilde x_	heta (0))} \ &\leq 2\sigma \sin \alpha + 2\sigma \sin \alpha + \sqrt{2}\sigma \ &\leq \sqrt{2}\sigma + 4\sigma \sin \alpha \end{align*} Since $\|w\| \leq \sqrt{2}\sigma + \mathcal{O}(\sin \alpha)$ we have from Eq. \eqref{eq:norm_H^w_bound} \[ \|\mathcal{H}^w\| \leq  rac{\sqrt{2}\sigma}{	au} + \mathcal{O}( rac{\sigma\sin \alpha}{	au}) \]
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.11
nodes.statement_short: Bound directional Hessians by tangent-variation (Lemmas 7.10, 9.14, 9.18), then bound $\|w\|\le\sqrt2\sigma+O(\sigma\sin\alpha)$.

nodes.statement:
We denote the tensor Hessian of $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^{D-d}$ at $\wtilde x_\theta(0)$ by $\mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta(0)):\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$. 
For brevity of notation, throughout this proof we will use $\mathcal{H}$ instead of $\mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta(0))$. For any chosen direction $u\in \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$ (i.e., a unit vector), $\mathcal{H}$ can be thought of as a function:
$\mathcal{H} ^u:\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$
defined as $\mathcal{H} ^u(v_1,v_2) = \lrangle{\mathcal{H} (v_1,v_2), u}$. 
We note that this definition is consistent with the definition of $\mathcal{H} f(\wtilde x_\theta(0))^u$ in \eqref{eq:H_w_def}.
Given $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $\norm{v} = 1$ we also define $\mathcal{H}_v:\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$
as $\mathcal{H}_v(\cdot) = \mathcal{H}(v,\cdot)$.
Note, that for any $w\in \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$ 
\[
{\|\mathcal{H}^w\|_{op}} = {\sup\limits_{v_1, v_2\in \mathbb{S}^{d}}|\lrangle{\mathcal{H}(v_1, v_2), w}|} 
\leq \sup\limits_{v_1, v_2\in \mathbb{S}^{d}}\|\mathcal{H}(v_1, v_2)\|_2\norm{w}_2
= \norm{w}_2\sup_{v\in\mathbb{S}^d}\|\mathcal{H}_v\|_{op}
,\]
where the right-most equality is true since $\mathcal{H}$ is symmetric.
nodes.name: Hessian notation
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $\mathcal H^u$, $\mathcal H_v$ and reduce to bounding $\|\mathcal H_v\|$.

nodes.statement:
Thus, in essence, we need to bound $\|\mathcal{H}_v\|_{op}$ for an arbitrary $v$. 
From the definition of $\mathcal{H}_v$ we know that 
\[
\mathcal{H}_v\ =  \lim_{t\to 0} \frac{\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_\theta(0)] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_\theta(0) + tv]}{t} 
.\]
Then, from Lemma \ref{lem:alpha-beta_x_no_func}  we have for small $t$
\[
\sin(\angle_{\max} (T_{\wtilde x_\theta}f,T_{\wtilde x_\theta + tv}f))\leq \frac{t}{\tau}(1+\tan^2\beta)+\mathcal{O}(t^2/\tau^2)
\]
where $\beta = \angle_{\max}(T_{\wtilde x_\theta}f,H)$. 
Therefore, applying Lemma \ref{lem:norm_from_angle} we get 
\[
 \|\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_\theta(0)] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde x_\theta(0) + tv] \|_{op} \leq \frac{t}{\tau}(1+\tan^2\beta)(1+\sin \beta) + \mathcal{O}(t^2/\tau^2)
,\]
and we get 
\[
\|\mathcal{H}_v\| \leq  \frac{1}{\tau}(1+\tan^2\beta)(1+\sin \beta)
.\]
Furthermore, from Lemma \ref{lem:alpha_beta_D} we know 
\[
\beta \leq \alpha + 3\alpha\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}
,\]
and so,
\[
\|\mathcal{H}_v\| \leq  \frac{1}{\tau}(1+\tan^2
\left(\alpha + 3\alpha\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\right))(1+\sin \left(\alpha + 3\alpha\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\right))
= \frac{1}{\tau} + \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sin \alpha}{\tau})
.\]
Thus, we obtain
\begin{equation} \|\mathcal{H}^w\| \leq \|w\| \left(\frac{1}{\tau} + \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sin \alpha}{\tau})\right)    
.\end{equation}
nodes.name: Bound $\mathcal H_v$
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 7.10, 9.14 and 9.18 give $\|\mathcal H_v\|\le 1/\tau+O(\sin\alpha/\tau)$.

nodes.statement: \|\mathcal{H}^w\| \leq \|w\| \left(\frac{1}{\tau} + \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sin \alpha}{\tau})\right) .
nodes.name: Equation (104) [eq:norm_H^w_bound]
nodes.label: eq:norm_H^w_bound

nodes.statement:
Hence, all we are left with is bounding  $\|w(0,\wtilde x_\theta (0))\|$. 
From Eq. \eqref{eq:def_w}, Lemma \ref{lem:bounding_stuff}, and Lemma \ref{lem:Dxtildew+Dxw}, we have 
\begin{align*}
    \|w(0,\wtilde x_\theta(0))\| &=\|f(0) - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)) + \theta \left(- f(0)\cdot \theta + f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)) \cdot \theta + 
    \sqrt{\Delta(0,\wtilde x_\theta (0))}\right)\|
    \\
    &\leq \|f(0) - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0))\| + \left|(- f(0) + f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0))) \cdot \theta\right| + 
    \sqrt{\Delta(0,\wtilde x_\theta (0))}
    \\
    &\leq 2\sigma \sin \alpha + 2\sigma \sin \alpha + \sqrt{2}\sigma 
    \\
    &\leq \sqrt{2}\sigma  + 4\sigma \sin \alpha 
\end{align*}

Since $\|w\| \leq \sqrt{2}\sigma + \mathcal{O}(\sin \alpha)$ 
we have from Eq. \eqref{eq:norm_H^w_bound}
\[
\|\mathcal{H}^w\| \leq \frac{\sqrt{2}\sigma}{\tau} + \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma\sin \alpha}{\tau})
\]
nodes.name: Bound $\|w\|$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|w\|$ and conclude.

nodes.statement: Let the conditions of Lemma \ref{lem:bound_J} hold, let $w(x, \wtilde x_\theta)$ be as defined in \eqref{eq:def_w}, $\wtilde x_\theta(x)$ be as defined in \eqref{eq:x_tilde_def}, and $\Delta$ as defined in \eqref{eq:Delta}. Denote by $\mathcal{D}^x_w, \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_w$ the partial differentials of $w$ with respect to the variables $x$ and $\wtilde x_\theta$. Then, for $\alpha$ smaller than some constant \begin{equation} \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2 \leq \Delta(0,\wtilde x_\theta (0)) \leq 2 \sigma^2 ,\end{equation} \begin{equation} \| \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_ w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)] \| \leq \mathcal{O}(\sin \alpha) \qquad \|\mathcal{D}^x_w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)]\| \leq \mathcal{O}(\sin \alpha) ,\end{equation} and \begin{equation} \| \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)] + \mathcal{D}^x_w[0, \wtilde x_\theta(0)]\| \leq \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}\sin \alpha) .\end{equation}

otag\ &\geq \sigma^2 -\|\wtilde{x}_	heta(0)\|^2 - 2\|f(0)- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0)) \|^2 
otag\ &\geq \sigma^2 -2\sigma^2 \sin^2 \alpha - 4\sigma^2 \sin^2 \alpha 
otag\ &\geq \sigma^2(1-6\sin^2 \alpha ) 
otag\ &\geq  rac{1}{2} \sigma^2 .\end{align} Similarly,  egin{align} \Delta(0,\wtilde x_	heta (0)) &= \sigma^2 + (f(0)^T 	heta - f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0))^T 	heta)^2 - \|0- \wtilde{x}_	heta(0)\|^2 - \|f(0)- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0)) \|^2 
otag\ &\leq \sigma^2 +\|\wtilde{x}_	heta(0)\|^2 + 2\|f(0)- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0)) \|^2 
otag\ &\leq \sigma^2 +2\sigma^2 \sin^2 \alpha + 4\sigma^2 \sin^2 \alpha 
otag\ &\leq \sigma^2(1+6\sin^2 \alpha ) 
otag\ &\geq 2 \sigma^2 .\end{align} and thus we showed Eq. \eqref{eq:Delta_bound}. Next we compute $\mathcal{D}^x_w$ and $D^{\wtilde{x}}_ w$  egin{align}  egin{split} \mathcal{D}^x_w =& \mathcal{D}_f[x] + 	heta {(	heta^T \mathcal{D}_f[x])} \ &~~+ { rac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}}} 	heta \left( 2 {(f(x)\cdot 	heta - f(\wtilde{x}_	heta) \cdot 	heta)}{	heta^T \mathcal{D}_f[x]} - 2(x- \wtilde{x}_	heta)^T - 2(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta))^T\mathcal{D}_f[x] ight)\ =&\left(I_{D-d} + 	heta 	heta^T +  rac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} 	heta \left( 2 (f(x)^T- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta)^T ) (	heta 	heta^T - I_{D-d} ) ight)ight) \mathcal{D}_f[x] -  rac{2}{\sqrt{\Delta}} 	heta (x- \wtilde{x}_	heta)^T \end{split} ,\end{align}  egin{align}  egin{split} \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_	heta}_ w = & -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_	heta] - 	heta {(	heta^T \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_	heta])} \ &~~+ { rac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}}} 	heta \left( -2 {(f(x)\cdot 	heta - f(\wtilde{x}_	heta) \cdot 	heta)}{	heta^T \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_	heta]} + 2(x- \wtilde{x}_	heta)^T + 2(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta))^T\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_	heta] ight)\ =&-\left(I_{D-d} + 	heta 	heta^T +  rac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} 	heta \left( 2 (f(x)^T- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta)^T ) (	heta 	heta^T - I_{D-d} ) ight)ight) \mathcal{D}_f[x] +  rac{2}{\sqrt{\Delta}} 	heta (x- \wtilde{x}_	heta)^T \end{split} .\end{align} From Eq. \eqref{eq:D_xw}, Lemma ef{lem:bounding_stuff}, and Eq. \eqref{eq:Delta_bound}, we have that  egin{align*} \|\mathcal{D}^x_w[0,\wtilde x_	heta(0)]\| \leq& \|I_{D-d} + 	heta 	heta^T +  rac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} 	heta \left( 2 (f(0)^T- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0))^T ) (	heta 	heta^T - I_{D-d} ) ight)\|_{op} \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]\|_{op} \ &~~+  rac{2}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \|(0- \wtilde{x}_	heta(0))^T\|_2 \ \leq& \mathcal{O}( \sin \alpha) \end{align*} Similarly, from Eq. \eqref{eq:D_xwtilde}, Lemma ef{lem:bounding_stuff}, and Eq. \eqref{eq:Delta_bound}, we have that  egin{equation} \|\mathcal{D}^x_w[0,\wtilde x_	heta(0)]\| \leq \mathcal{O}( \sin \alpha) \end{equation} Thus, we showed \eqref{eq:Dws_bound}. Now we show \eqref{eq:Dxtildew+Dxw_bound}. From \eqref{eq:D_xw} and \eqref{eq:D_xwtilde} we have  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} \sigma \mathcal{D}^x_w + \sigma \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_	heta}_ w &= \mathcal{D}_f[x] -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_	heta] +	heta 	heta^T (\mathcal{D}_f[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_	heta]) \ &~~+ rac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} 	heta  igg( 2 (f(x)\cdot 	heta - f(\wtilde{x}_	heta) \cdot 	heta)	heta^T - 2(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta))^T igg) (\mathcal{D}_f[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_	heta])\ &= \left(I_{D-d} +	heta 	heta^T + rac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} 	heta  igg( 2 (f(x)^T - f(\wtilde{x}_	heta)^T)	heta	heta^T - 2(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta))^T igg)ight) (\mathcal{D}_f[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_	heta])\ &=\left(I_{D-d} +	heta 	heta^T + rac{2}{\sqrt{\Delta}} 	heta (f(x)^T - f(\wtilde{x}_	heta)^T) (	heta	heta^T - I_{D-d})ight) (\mathcal{D}_f[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_	heta]) \end{aligned} \end{equation} Since we are bounding for $x= 0 $, we have from Lemma ef{lem:bounding_stuff}, that $\|f(0) - f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0))\| \leq \mathcal{O}(\sigma \sin^2 \alpha)$, for $\alpha$ smaller than some constant. Taking the norm of \eqref{eq:D_xw-Dxwtilde} we have that \[ \|\sigma \mathcal{D}^x_w + \sigma \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_	heta}_ w \| \leq \left\|I_{D-d} +	heta 	heta^T + rac{2}{\sqrt{\Delta}} 	heta (f(x)^T - f(\wtilde{x}_	heta)^T) (	heta	heta^T - I_{D-d})ight\| \|\mathcal{D}_f[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_	heta]\| \] From Eq. \eqref{eq:Delta_bound} and Lemma ef{lem:Dfx-Dfxtilde} we have, \[ \|\sigma \mathcal{D}^x_w + \sigma \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_	heta}_ w \| = \mathcal{O}( rac{\sigma}{	au}\sin \alpha) \]
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.12
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\Delta$ by Lemma 9.15, compute the partial differentials of $w$ explicitly and bound them; their sum involves only $Df(x)-Df(\tilde x_\theta)$ (Lemma 9.13).

nodes.statement:
First we bound $\Delta$ from Eq. \eqref{eq:Delta} at $x=0,\wtilde x_\theta = x_\theta(0)$ using Lemma \ref{lem:bounding_stuff}, and assuming $\alpha$ is smaller than some constant.
\begin{align}
\Delta(0,\wtilde x_\theta (0)) &= \sigma^2 + (f(0)^T \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0))^T \theta)^2 - \|0- \wtilde{x}_\theta(0)\|^2 - \|f(0)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)) \|^2 
\notag\\
&\geq \sigma^2 -\|\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)\|^2 - 2\|f(0)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)) \|^2
\notag\\
&\geq \sigma^2 -2\sigma^2 \sin^2 \alpha - 4\sigma^2 \sin^2 \alpha 
\notag\\
&\geq \sigma^2(1-6\sin^2 \alpha )
\notag\\
&\geq \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2
.\end{align}
Similarly, 
\begin{align}
\Delta(0,\wtilde x_\theta (0)) &= \sigma^2 + (f(0)^T \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0))^T \theta)^2 - \|0- \wtilde{x}_\theta(0)\|^2 - \|f(0)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)) \|^2 
\notag\\
&\leq \sigma^2 +\|\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)\|^2 + 2\|f(0)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0)) \|^2
\notag\\
&\leq \sigma^2 +2\sigma^2 \sin^2 \alpha + 4\sigma^2 \sin^2 \alpha 
\notag\\
&\leq \sigma^2(1+6\sin^2 \alpha )
\notag\\
&\geq 2 \sigma^2
.\end{align}
and thus we showed Eq. \eqref{eq:Delta_bound}.
nodes.name: Bound $\Delta$
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 9.15 gives $\sigma^2/2\le\Delta\le2\sigma^2$.

otag\ &\geq \sigma^2 -\|\wtilde{x}_	heta(0)\|^2 - 2\|f(0)- f(\wtilde{x}_	heta(0)) \|^2

nodes.statement:
Next we compute $\mathcal{D}^x_w$ and $D^{\wtilde{x}}_ w$
\begin{align} \begin{split}
     \mathcal{D}^x_w =& \mathcal{D}_f[x] 
    +
    \theta {(\theta^T \mathcal{D}_f[x])} \\
    &~~+
    {\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}}} \theta \left( 
    2 {(f(x)\cdot \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \cdot \theta)}{\theta^T \mathcal{D}_f[x]} 
    - 
    2(x- \wtilde{x}_\theta)^T 
    - 
    2(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta))^T\mathcal{D}_f[x]  \right)\\
    =&\left(I_{D-d} 
    +
    \theta \theta^T  
    +
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \theta \left( 
    2 (f(x)^T- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T ) (\theta \theta^T - I_{D-d} )
      \right)\right) \mathcal{D}_f[x] -
    \frac{2}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \theta (x- \wtilde{x}_\theta)^T 
    \end{split}
,\end{align}

\begin{align} \begin{split}
    \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_ w = & -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta] 
    - 
    \theta {(\theta^T \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta])} \\
    &~~+
    {\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}}} \theta \left( 
    -2 {(f(x)\cdot \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \cdot \theta)}{\theta^T \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]} 
    + 
    2(x- \wtilde{x}_\theta)^T 
    +
    2(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta))^T\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]  \right)\\
    =&-\left(I_{D-d} 
    +
    \theta \theta^T  
    +
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \theta \left( 
    2 (f(x)^T- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T ) (\theta \theta^T - I_{D-d} )
      \right)\right) \mathcal{D}_f[x] +
    \frac{2}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \theta (x- \wtilde{x}_\theta)^T 
    \end{split}
.\end{align}
From Eq. \eqref{eq:D_xw}, Lemma \ref{lem:bounding_stuff}, and Eq. \eqref{eq:Delta_bound},  we have that 
\begin{align*}
     \|\mathcal{D}^x_w[0,\wtilde x_\theta(0)]\| \leq& 
    \|I_{D-d} 
    +
    \theta \theta^T  
    +
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \theta \left( 
    2 (f(0)^T- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0))^T ) (\theta \theta^T - I_{D-d} )
      \right)\|_{op} \|\mathcal{D}_f[0]\|_{op} \\
      &~~+
    \frac{2}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \|(0- \wtilde{x}_\theta(0))^T\|_2 
    \\
    \leq& \mathcal{O}( \sin \alpha)
\end{align*}
Similarly, from Eq. \eqref{eq:D_xwtilde}, Lemma \ref{lem:bounding_stuff}, and Eq. \eqref{eq:Delta_bound},  we have that 
\begin{equation}
     \|\mathcal{D}^x_w[0,\wtilde x_\theta(0)]\| 
    \leq \mathcal{O}( \sin \alpha)
\end{equation}
Thus, we showed \eqref{eq:Dws_bound}.

Now we show \eqref{eq:Dxtildew+Dxw_bound}. From \eqref{eq:D_xw} and \eqref{eq:D_xwtilde} we have 
\begin{equation} \begin{aligned}
    \sigma \mathcal{D}^x_w + \sigma \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_ w 
    &= \mathcal{D}_f[x] -\mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta] +\theta \theta^T (\mathcal{D}_f[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]) \\
    &~~+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \theta 
    \bigg( 2 (f(x)\cdot \theta - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta) \cdot \theta)\theta^T - 2(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta))^T\bigg) (\mathcal{D}_f[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta])\\
    &= \left(I_{D-d} +\theta \theta^T +\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \theta 
    \bigg( 2 (f(x)^T - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T)\theta\theta^T - 2(f(x)- f(\wtilde{x}_\theta))^T\bigg)\right) (\mathcal{D}_f[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta])\\
    &=\left(I_{D-d} +\theta \theta^T +\frac{2}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \theta 
      (f(x)^T - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T) (\theta\theta^T - I_{D-d})\right) (\mathcal{D}_f[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta])
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Since we are bounding for $x= 0 $, we have from Lemma \ref{lem:bounding_stuff}, that $\|f(0) - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta(0))\| \leq \mathcal{O}(\sigma \sin^2 \alpha)$, for $\alpha$ smaller than some constant.
Taking the norm of \eqref{eq:D_xw-Dxwtilde} we have that 
\[
\|\sigma \mathcal{D}^x_w + \sigma \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_ w \| \leq \left\|I_{D-d} +\theta \theta^T +\frac{2}{\sqrt{\Delta}} \theta 
      (f(x)^T - f(\wtilde{x}_\theta)^T) (\theta\theta^T - I_{D-d})\right\| \|\mathcal{D}_f[x] - \mathcal{D}_f[\wtilde{x}_\theta]\|
\]
From Eq. \eqref{eq:Delta_bound} and Lemma \ref{lem:Dfx-Dfxtilde} we have,
\[
\|\sigma \mathcal{D}^x_w + \sigma \mathcal{D}^{\wtilde{x}_\theta}_ w \| =  \mathcal{O}(\frac{\sigma}{\tau}\sin \alpha)
\]

nodes.statement: Let $L_1, L_2$ be two linear operators from $H$ a $d$-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb{R}^D$ to $\mathbb{R}^{D-d}$. Let, $\angle_{\max}(H,(H,L_1(H))_H) \leq \alpha$, where $(H,L_1(H)_H)$ is the subspace spanned by $H$ and $L_1(H)$, the target space of $L_1$. Furthermore, let $\angle_{\max}((H,L_1(H))_H,(H,L_2(H))_H) \leq \beta$. Then, \[\|L_1 - L_2\|_{op} \leq \sin \beta(1 + \sin\alpha).\]
nodes.name: Operator gap from angle between graphs
nodes.label: lem:norm_from_angle

nodes.statement: For any $x\in H, \|x\| = 1$, from Lemma \ref{lem:Q_angle_between_flats}, there is $y\in H$ such that \[ \|(x,L_1(x)) - (y,L_2(y))\| \leq \sin \beta .\] Therefore, \[ \|x-y\|^2+\|L_1(x) - L_2(y)\|^2 = \|(x,L_1(x)) - (y,L_2(y))\|^2\leq \sin^2 \beta ,\] and \[ \|x-y\| \leq \sin \beta ~,~ \|L_1(x) - L_2(y)\| \leq \sin\beta .\] Note, that $\|L_1(y) - L_1(x)\| \leq \|L_1\|_{op}\|x-y\|$. Since $\angle_{\max}(H,(H,L_1(H))) \leq \alpha$ we have that $\|L_1\|_{op}\leq \sin \alpha$, and we get that \[ \|L_1(y) - L_1(x)\| \leq \sin \alpha \sin \beta .\] Furthermore, \[ \|L_1(x) - L_2(x)\| = \|L_1(x) - L_1(y) + L_1(y) - L_2(x)\| \leq \|L_1(x) - L_1(y)\|+\|L_1(y) - L_2(x)\| ,\] and so \[ \|L_1(x) - L_2(x)\| \leq \sin \beta(1 + \sin\alpha) .\]

.\]

,\]

\[

.\]

.\]

	,\]

	\[

	and so we get
	\begin{align*}
	\lrbrackets{\beta - \alpha}^2 
	&\leq
	4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}sin\beta\lrbrackets{2\alpha   + \frac{\sigma}{\tau}sin\beta} \\
	\frac{\beta^2-2\alpha\beta + \alpha^2}{4} 
	&\leq 
	2 \frac{\sigma}{\tau}\alpha\beta + \frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}\beta^2
	,\end{align*}
	that can be written as the parabola 
	\begin{align*}
	\lrbrackets{\frac{1}{4} - \frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}}\beta^2 - \lrbrackets{\frac{1}{2} + 2 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha \beta + \frac{1}{4}\alpha^2 & \leq
	0 \\
	\lrbrackets{1 - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}}\beta^2 - \lrbrackets{2 + 8 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha \beta + \alpha^2 & \leq
	0 
	.\end{align*}
nodes.name: Quadratic inequality
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 9.17 yields a quadratic inequality in $\beta$.

nodes.name: Roots
nodes.statement_short: Compute the roots.

nodes.statement:
Therefore, from Remark \ref{rem:taylor_sqrt1-x2_clean} the inequality holds for
	\begin{align*}
	\beta 
	&\geq 
	\frac{\lrbrackets{1 +4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha - \lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha\sqrt{1 - \frac{\lrbrackets{1 - 4 \frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2} }}{\lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }^2}}}{1 - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}}\\
	&\geq
	\frac{\lrbrackets{1 +4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha - \lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha\lrbrackets{1 - \frac{\lrbrackets{1 - 4 \frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2} }}{\lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }^2}}}{1 - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}}\\
	&=
	\alpha\frac{1}{{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }} \\
	&\geq 
	\alpha - 4\alpha\frac{\sigma}{\tau}
	,\end{align*}
	where on the other hand
	\begin{align*}
	\beta 
	&\leq
	\frac{\lrbrackets{1 +4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha + \lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha\sqrt{1 - \frac{\lrbrackets{1 - 4 \frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2} }}{\lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }^2}}}{1 - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}} \\
	&=
	\frac{\lrbrackets{1 +4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha + \lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha\sqrt{1 - \frac{\lrbrackets{1 - 2 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\lrbrackets{1 + 2 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }}{\lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }^2}}}{1 - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}} \\
	&\leq
	\frac{\lrbrackets{1 +4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha + \lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha\sqrt{1 - \frac{\lrbrackets{1 - 2 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\lrbrackets{1 + 2 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }}{\lrbrackets{1 + 2 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }^2}}}{1 - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}} \\
	&=
	\frac{\lrbrackets{1 +4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha + \lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha\sqrt{1 - \frac{{1 - 2 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }}{{1 + 2 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }}}}{1 - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}} 
	,\end{align*}
	since we know that $ \frac{1}{1 + x} \geq 1 - x $ we get
	\begin{align*}
	\beta 
	&\leq
	\frac{\lrbrackets{1 +4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha + \lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha\sqrt{1 - \lrbrackets{1 - 2 \frac{\sigma}{\tau}}^2}}{1 - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}} \\
	&\leq
	\frac{\lrbrackets{1 +4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha + \lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha\sqrt{4\frac{\sigma}{\tau} - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}}}{1 - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}}\\
	&\leq
	\frac{\lrbrackets{1 +4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha + 2\lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}}{1 - 4\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}}
	,\end{align*}
	and by using the bound $ \frac{1}{1 - x^2} \leq 1 + 2 x^2 $ for $ 0 \leq x \leq 0.5 $	
	\begin{align*}
	\beta
	&\leq
	\lrbrackets{\lrbrackets{1 +4\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}\alpha + 2\lrbrackets{1 + 4 \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }\alpha\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}}\lrbrackets{1 + 8\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2}} \\
	&=
	\alpha + 2\alpha\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} + 4\alpha\frac{\sigma}{\tau} + 8 \alpha\frac{\sigma^{1.5}}{\tau^{1.5}} + 8\alpha\frac{\sigma^2}{\tau^2} + 16\alpha\frac{\sigma^{2.5}}{\tau^{2.5}} + 32\alpha\frac{\sigma^{3}}{\tau^{3}} + 32\alpha\frac{\sigma^{3.5}}{\tau^{3.5}}
	.\end{align*}
nodes.name: Bound the roots
nodes.statement_short: Taylor bounds on both roots.

nodes.statement:
Then, since $ \frac{\sigma}{\tau}\leq \frac{1}{36} $ is sufficiently small we obtain 
	\[
	\beta \leq \alpha + 3\alpha\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}
	,\]
	and 
	\[
	\alpha - 4\alpha\frac{\sigma}{\tau}  \leq \beta \leq \alpha + 3\alpha\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}
	\]

nodes.statement: Let $(q_\ell, H_\ell)$ be defined in Algorithm \ref{alg:step2_clean} and $ \pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}(x) $ be defined in \eqref{eq:argmin2_clean} and let $ H_{\ell + 1} = T_0 \pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell} $ the tangent to the graph of $ \pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell} $ at $ \pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}(0) $. Then, for all $ \delta>0 $ there is $ N_\delta $ such that for all $ n > N_\delta $ we have with probability $ 1-\delta $ \[ \angle_{\max}(T_0\wtilde f_\ell, H_{\ell + 1}) \leq 2\sqrt{d}\frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{n ^{r_1}} ,\] where ${r_1} = \frac{k-1}{2k + d}$ and $C_0$ is a constant.

nodes.statement: We first note that it is sufficient to bound the error of estimating the image of $\mathcal{D}_{\wtilde{f}_\ell}[0]$, the differential of $ \wtilde f_\ell(x) $ at 0, by the image of $ \mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}}[0] $, the differential of the local polynomial least-squares regression $\pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}$. Explicitly, if \[ \|{\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}}[0] - \mathcal{D}_{ \wtilde f_\ell}[0]}\|_{op} \leq \sqrt{d}\frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{n^{r_1}} ,\] then, by using Lemma \ref{lem:Diff_Tf_bound} we get that \[ \sin(\angle_{\max}(T_0\wtilde f_\ell, T_0\pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell})) \leq \sqrt{d}\frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{n^{r_1}} ,\] which for sufficiently large $ n $ yields \[ \angle_{\max}(T_0\wtilde f_\ell, T_0\pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}) \leq 2\sqrt{d}\frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{n^{r_1}} ,\] as required. Therefore, it is sufficient to show that for any $\delta$ there is $N_\delta$ such that for all $n>N_\delta$ we have \[ \|{\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}}[0] - \mathcal{D}_{ \wtilde f_\ell}[0]}\|_{op} \leq \sqrt{d}\frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{n^{r_1}} ,\] with probability of at least $1 - \delta$. Let us reiterate the minimization problem by which we derive the approximant. Namely, given a sample $ \{r_i\}_{i=1}^{n} $ drawn i.i.d from $ \text{Unif}(\mathcal{M}_\sigma) $, and a coordinate system $ (q, H)\in \mathbb{R}^D\times Gr(d,D) $ we look for a polynomial $ \pi^*_{q,H} $ minimizing \begin{equation} J_2(\pi ~|~ q, H) = \frac{1}{N_{q,H}}\sum_{r_i \in U_{\textrm{ROI}}^{n}} \norm{r_i - \pi(x_i)}^2 ,\end{equation} where $x_i$ are the projections of $r_i - q$ onto $H$, and $U_{\textrm{ROI}}^{n}(q,H)$ is defined through a bandwidth $\epsilon_{n}$ as \begin{equation} U_{\textrm{ROI}}^{n}(q,H) = {\{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}~|~\operatorname{dist}(x_i, q)<\epsilon_{n}\}} ,\end{equation} and $N_{q,H}$ denotes the number of samples in $U_{\textrm{ROI}}^{n}(q, H)$. Explicitly, \begin{equation} \pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell} = \arg\!\min_{\pi\in \Pi_{k-1}^{d\mapsto D}} J_2(\pi ~|~ q_\ell, H_\ell) .\end{equation} We demand that the bandwidth $\epsilon_{n}\to 0$ as ${n}\to\infty$ such that \begin{equation} 0<\lim_{{n}\rightarrow\infty}N^{1/(2k+1)}\cdot \epsilon_{n} < \infty .\end{equation} And, the approximation is defined through $\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}}[0]$ From Lemma \ref{lem:noise_cov_bound} we can apply Theorem 3.2 from \cite{aizenbud2021VectorEstimation} that gives convergence rates for local polynomial regression of vector valued functions in our case. Thus, we have that for every direction in the basis $\{x^j\}_{j=1}^d\subset H_\ell$ and every $\delta$ there exists $N_{\delta}$ such that for all $n > N_{\delta}$ we have \[ \Pr(\|{\partial_{x^j} \pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}(0) - \partial_{x^j} \wtilde f_\ell(0)}\| > \frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)^{r_1}}{n^{r_1}}) < \delta ,\] where $r_1 = \frac{k-1}{2k + d}$ and $C_0$ is a constant. Notice that $r_1 \leq 1/2$, and thus \[ \Pr(\|{\partial_{x^j} \pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}(0) - \partial_{x^j} \wtilde f_\ell(0)}\| > \frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{n^{r_1}}) < \delta .\] Thus, taking into account all $d$ directions of the basis to $H_\ell$ we get that there are $C$ and $N_\delta$ such that for all $n > N_\delta$ \[ \Pr(\|{\partial_{x^j} \pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}(0) - \partial_{x^j} \wtilde f_\ell(0)}\| > \frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{n^{r_1}}\textrm{ for any } 1 \leq j \leq d) < d\delta ,\] and thus \[ \Pr(\|{\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}}[0] - \mathcal{D}_{\wtilde f_\ell}[0]}\|_{op} > \sqrt{d}\frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{n^r}) < d\delta ,\] as required.

From Lemma \ref{lem:noise_cov_bound} we can apply Theorem 3.2 from \cite{aizenbud2021VectorEstimation} that gives convergence rates for local polynomial regression of vector valued functions in our case. Thus, we have that for every direction in the basis $\{x^j\}_{j=1}^d\subset H_\ell$ and every $\delta$ there exists  $N_{\delta}$ such that for all $n > N_{\delta}$ we have
\[
\Pr(\|{\partial_{x^j} \pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}(0) - \partial_{x^j} \wtilde f_\ell(0)}\| > \frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)^{r_1}}{n^{r_1}}) < \delta

where $r_1 = \frac{k-1}{2k + d}$ and $C_0$ is a constant. Notice that $r_1 \leq 1/2$, and thus

\Pr(\|{\partial_{x^j} \pi^*_{q_\ell, H_\ell}(0) - \partial_{x^j} \wtilde f_\ell(0)}\| > \frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{n^{r_1}}) < \delta
.\]
Thus, taking into account all $d$ directions of the basis to $H_\ell$ we get that there are $C$ and $N_\delta$ such that for all $n > N_\delta$

nodes.statement: Let $H_\ell\in Gr(d, D)$, and let $f_\ell:H_\ell\simeq\mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$, defined as in \eqref{eq:fl_def}. Let $\eta_\ell$ defined in \eqref{eq:ftilde_def}. Denote $\alpha_\ell = \angle_{\max} (T_0f_{\ell}, H_{\ell})$ and assume $\alpha_\ell<1/D^{1/4}$. Then, \[ \|\mathrm{cov}(\eta_\ell)\|_{op} \leq \sqrt{\frac{c\sigma}{D-d}} \]

assumptions: assume $\alpha_\ell<1/D^{1/4}$

nodes.statement: For ease of notation, denote $\wtilde{D} = D-d$. Since we are interested in bounding \begin{equation} \|\mathrm{cov}(\eta_\ell) \|_{op} = \max_{\vec{x}\in \mathbb{S}_{\wtilde{D} - 1} } \vec{x}^T \mathrm{cov}(\eta_\ell)\vec{x} \end{equation} we note that \[ \vec{x}^T\mathrm{cov}(\eta_\ell)\vec{x} = \mbox{Var}(\eta_\ell\cdot \vec x) .\] Thus, rewriting \eqref{eq:cov_norm} we have \begin{equation} \|\mathrm{cov}(\eta_\ell)\|_{op}= \max_{\vec{x}\in \mathbb{S}_{\wtilde{D} - 1}} \vec{x}^T\mathrm{cov}(\eta_\ell)\vec{x} = \max_{\vec{x}\in \mathbb{S}_{\wtilde{D} - 1}}\mbox{Var}(\eta_\ell\cdot \vec{x}) \leq \max_{\vec{x}\in \mathbb{S}_{\wtilde{D} - 1}}\mathbb{E}((\eta_\ell\cdot \vec{x})^2) \end{equation} Thus, our goal is to bound, for any $\vec{z}\in \mathbb{S}_{\wtilde{D} - 1}$ the expression $\mathbb{E}((\eta_\ell\cdot \vec{z})^2)$. From the definition of $g$ and $\Omega$ in \eqref{eq:g_def} and \eqref{eq:Omega_def}, we have that \begin{align} \mathbb{E}((\eta_\ell\cdot \vec{z})^2) &= \frac{\int\limits_{y\in\Omega(x)} (y \cdot \vec{z})^2 dy}{\int\limits_{y\in\Omega(x)} dy} = \frac{\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D - 1}}\int\limits_0^{g(x,\theta)} (\theta \cdot \vec{z})^2 r^2 r^{\wtilde D-1} drd\theta}{\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D - 1}}\int\limits_0^{g(x,\theta)} r^{\wtilde D-1} drd\theta} \notag\\ & = \frac{\wtilde D\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D - 1}}(\theta \cdot \vec{z})^2 g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D+2} d\theta}{(\wtilde D+2)\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D - 1}}g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} drd\theta} ,\end{align} where $dr$ is the measure over the radial component, $r^{\wtilde D-1}$ is the Jacobian introduced by the change of variables and $d\theta$ is the measure over the $(\wtilde D-1)$-dimensional sphere. Following the rationale of the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:bound_Df-Dfwtilde}, we split $\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}$ into $\Omega_1$ and $\Omega_2$ of \eqref{eq:Omegas_def}. That is, \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \Omega_1 &= \{\theta~|~0\leq \vec{z}^T\theta \leq \xi\}\\ \Omega_2 &= \{\theta~|~\vec{z}^T\theta > \xi\} \end{aligned} ,\end{equation*} for some $\xi$ to be chosen later. Thus, denoting $z = \theta^T \vec{z}$ we rewrite \eqref{eq:E(Z_z)} as` \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}((\eta_\ell\cdot \vec{z})^2) &=\frac{\wtilde D\left(\int\limits_{\Omega_1}z^2 g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D+2} d\theta + \int\limits_{\Omega_2}z^2 g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D+2} d\theta\right)}{(\wtilde D+2)\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} d\theta} \\ &\leq \frac{\wtilde D\left(\xi^2 \int\limits_{\Omega_1} g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D+2} d\theta + \int\limits_{\Omega_2} g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D+2} d\theta\right)}{(\wtilde D+2)\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} d\theta} \end{align*} Since the conditions of Lemma \ref{lem:g_bond_weak} are met, we have $\sigma \leq g(0,\theta)\leq \sigma + 4\sigma \alpha_\ell ^2$, and thus \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}((\eta_\ell\cdot \vec{z})^2) &\leq \frac{\wtilde D\left(\xi^2 \int\limits_{\Omega_1} g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D+2} d\theta + \int\limits_{\Omega_2} g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D+2} d\theta\right)}{(\wtilde D+2)\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} d\theta} \\ &\leq \frac{\wtilde D\sigma^2(1+4\alpha_\ell ^2)^2\left(\xi^2 \int\limits_{\Omega_1} g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} d\theta + \int\limits_{\Omega_2} g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} d\theta\right)}{(\wtilde D+2)\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} d\theta} \\ &\leq \frac{\wtilde D\sigma^2(1+4\alpha_\ell ^2)^2}{\wtilde D+2}\left(\xi^2 +\frac{ \int\limits_{\Omega_2} g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} d\theta}{\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}}g(x,\theta)^{\wtilde D} d\theta} \right) \\ &\leq \frac{\wtilde D\sigma^2(1+4\alpha_\ell ^2)^2}{\wtilde D+2}\left(\xi^2 +\frac{\sigma^{\wtilde D}(1+4\alpha_\ell ^2)^{\wtilde D} \int\limits_{\Omega_2} d\theta}{\sigma^{\wtilde D}\int\limits_{\mathbb{S}_{\wtilde D-1}} d\theta} \right) \\ &\leq \frac{\wtilde D\sigma^2(1+4\alpha_\ell ^2)^2}{\wtilde D+2}\left(\xi^2 +\frac{(1+4\alpha_\ell ^2)^{\wtilde D}}{\xi\sqrt{\wtilde D-1}} e^{-(\wtilde D-1)\xi^2/2}\right) ,\end{align*} where the last inequality comes from Eq. \eqref{eq:Omega3_to_ball_ratio}. Since $\alpha_\ell <1/D^{1/4}$ we have that $(1+4\alpha_\ell ^2)^{\wtilde D}$ is bounded by some constant $c$. Choosing $\xi = 2\sqrt{\frac{\log(\wtilde D-1)}{\wtilde D-1}}$ we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}((\eta_\ell\cdot \vec{z})^2) &\leq \frac{\wtilde D\sigma^2(1+4\alpha_\ell ^2)^2 }{\wtilde D+2}\left(4\frac{\log(\wtilde D-1)}{\wtilde D-1} +\frac{c}{2\sqrt{\log(\wtilde D-1)}} (\wtilde D-1)^{-2}\right) \\ &\leq c_1\sigma^2\frac{\log(\wtilde D-1)}{\wtilde D-1}\leq \sqrt{\frac{c\sigma}{\wtilde D}} \end{align*} for some constants $c,c_1$. Combining with Eq. \eqref{eq:cov_norm2}, we conclude the proof.
